entities.summary:
Cornelius (b. 180 CE, Rome) was a prominent entrepreneur or business leader of the Classical era, active in Rome and known for his religious figures connections. He played a significant role in shaping the city's commercial landscape, fostering economic growth and development. Through his entrepreneurial ventures, Cornelius contributed to the establishment of several major institutions, including temples and public buildings. His influence extended beyond Rome, as he was involved in trade and commerce with neighboring regions. As a result of his business acumen and religious connections, Cornelius left a lasting legacy in the city of Rome.

Cornelius's significance lies in his ability to navigate the complexities of the Roman economy, leveraging his connections to the religious elite to secure funding and support for his ventures. His success was not limited to Rome, as he was also involved in trade with other regions, including the eastern provinces.

In terms of his legacy, Cornelius is remembered as a skilled businessman and religious figure, whose contributions to the city of Rome continue to be felt today.

Cornelius's entrepreneurial spirit and religious connections make him a fascinating figure in the history of ancient Rome.
